name: Credo Technology Group Holding Ltd
sector: Semiconductors (high-speed connectivity: AEC, optical DSPs, PCIe retimers for AI/datacenter)
businessSummary: Designs high-speed connectivity chips (Active Electrical Cables, optical DSPs, retimers, SerDes IP) primarily for hyperscaler AI/datacenter networking.

price.note: Down 8.21% on the day; ~61% below its 52-week high.

netDebt.note: Net cash $813.6M, no borrowings line disclosed; not current.

enterpriseValue.note: Stale relative to Nov 16 price decline.

fcfTTM.note: Not disclosed in press releases reviewed.

beta5y.note: Very high -- consistent with realized volatility.

consensus.note: Stale -- implies ~130% upside, likely not reset; press reports analyst target cuts (e.g. BofA to $160).

recentEvents: Q2 FY2026 (reported Dec 2025): revenue $268.0M +272.1% YoY from $72.0M.
Q1 FY2027 (reported Sep 2026): revenue $479M +115% YoY -- growth decelerated sharply from +272%.
Q1 FY27 GAAP gross margin fell to 64.5% from 67.4% a year earlier.
Stock down ~61% from its 52-week high; fell 8.2% on Nov 16, 2026 alone.
Press coverage references analyst target cuts (e.g. BofA to $160) and customer-concentration concerns.
valueTrapFlags: Trailing P/E still 42.6x even after the drawdown -- valuation not fully normalized.
Growth decelerating fast: +272% to ~+115% YoY; next guided quarter implies further deceleration.
GAAP gross margin compression (-2.9pts YoY) alongside the deceleration.
Consensus target ($277) appears stale vs. more recent analyst cuts -- don't trust at face value.
growthQualityNotes: Growth confirmed real from primary-source quarterly releases across 5 consecutive quarters.
Gross margins remain healthy (mid-60s% GAAP) and non-GAAP operating margin strong (48.2% Q1 FY27).
Net cash balance sheet, no debt disclosed.
Key open question: whether deceleration toward 'normal' growth continues and whether that's priced in after the 61% drawdown.
dataGaps: FCF, EV/EBIT, ROIC, ROE, interest coverage not found.
Current post-decline EV/EBITDA, FCF yield unavailable.

valuation.method: EPS-based scenario fair value off TTM EPS, explicitly built around the confirmed sharp growth deceleration and the still-rich post-drawdown multiple

bear.note: Growth decelerates further toward normal semiconductor-industry rates, multiple fully normalizes.

base.note: Growth settles around 40-60% YoY (down from 115%) as AI networking demand remains strong but less explosive.

bull.note: AI datacenter networking demand reaccelerates, Credo wins additional hyperscaler sockets.

valuation.whyItFits: Confirmed real hypergrowth from primary filings (not hype) in AI datacenter connectivity, net-cash balance sheet, healthy gross margins even as growth decelerates -- included as a higher-risk, already-partially-derated growth name rather than a clean bargain.
valuation.growthDrivers: AI/datacenter high-speed connectivity (AEC, optical DSP, retimers) demand from hyperscaler buildouts.
valuation.saturation: Growth has already decelerated sharply (+272% to +115% YoY) and next-quarter guidance implies further deceleration -- the hypergrowth phase looks to be ending.
valuation.principalRisk: Customer concentration among a small number of hyperscalers, and a valuation that -- even after a 61% drawdown -- still assumes continued strong growth.
